newsitem.title: CANADA: Separatists say Quebec sovereignty is inevitable.
newsitem.headline: Separatists say Quebec sovereignty is inevitable.

text.p: A leading Quebec separatist said on Tuesday that sovereignty was the only credible option for the French-speaking province despite defeat in a referendum on the issue one year ago.

"There is no doubt that sovereignty embodies more than ever the sole credible option for our future, that it is the logical step on our path as a people," said Michel Gauthier, leader of the Bloc Quebecois in the federal Parliament.

"We must prepare the rest of Canada for this inevitable reality...I am confident that on the eve of the year 2000, Quebeckers will soon choose the path of the future, the one by which we will finally be able to take our potential to the limit."

His remarks came in a statement which he planned to deliver on Wednesday, exactly a year after Quebec voters narrowly voted against seceding from Canada and seeking some form of economic or political partnership with the country.
He made it clear that the partnership route, which many Quebeckers view as less threatening than breaking away from Canada, was the option preferred by the Bloc.
"The partnership which is intimately tied to the future of a sovereign Quebec must spearhead our future relations with Canada," he said.
The federal government has made it clear that it would force any future referendum to ask a simpler question -- do you want Quebec to leave Canada or not.
Gauthier, who took over leadership of the Bloc from firebrand Lucien Bouchard after Bouchard became Quebec's premier, accused the Ottawa government of failing to deliver on promises of change.
"Therefore, we must take action and prepare our collective future right now," he said.
Quebec law prohibits the holding of another referendum on sovereignty until provincial elections -- which are not due for another three years -- are held.
